source.title: Scaling White-Box Transformers for Vision
source.authors: Jinrui Yang; Xian-Hang Li; Druv Pai; Yu-Yin Zhou; Yi Ma; Yao-Dong Yu; Ci-Hang Xie

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports validation cross-entropy for two CRATE-α language-model sizes, directly measuring loss against parameter count, but does not fit a scaling law. Its larger study extends scaling experiments to vision.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports classification, transfer, and zero-shot image results across model scales. These bear on V6. The language-model loss results bear on V1, but cover only two sizes and do not fit or test a power law over several orders of magnitude. Training-loss curves in Figures 3, 4, and 8–10 are not extracted as numeric results because they are plots without reported numeric values; the paper describes some trends in text. Table 3 compares models but does not test a size-scaling trend. Cited CRATE and GPT-2 results in Table 4 are not treated as the paper's own results.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper. It shows that its CRATE-α variant improves from Base to Large to Huge on vision tasks. It fits no power law, checks no predictability, and tests no compute allocation. Its only language-model result is two sizes trained for different fractions of their schedule (80% vs 55%). The size comparisons report the gains of the authors' own method; they do not test any version of the scaling-law claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CRATE-α can be scaled in model size and data for vision while keeping interpretability, and they fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce the original language-model scaling-law fitting procedure. It modifies CRATE, scales vision and language model configurations, and reports task accuracy and a small number of validation-loss results without fitting scaling exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with patch size and training setup; the paper reports different results for ImageNet pre-training/fine-tuning and DataComp1B vision-language pre-training/fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla CRATE gains only +0.5% from B to L, while CRATE-α gains 1.9–4.0% from B to L (and more from L to H). Scalability depends on the sparse-coding block design.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether accuracy improves with model size depends on the architecture: some architectures show diminishing returns where modified ones keep improving.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that ImageNet-21K training loss improves predictably with model capacity (Figure 3), but give no numbers or fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision-transformer training loss decreases with model size (qualitative).

record.problems: The language-loss comparison includes only two CRATE-α sizes, trained for different fractions of the planned iterations. No scaling-law fit, uncertainty estimates, fixed-compute allocation study, or run-to-run comparisons are reported. The vision training-loss curves are presented as plots rather than numeric values. Table 6's flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of its individual metric values.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss curves in Figures 3, 4, and 8–10 are not extracted because the plotted values are not numerically stated; the text gives qualitative descriptions. Table 6's individual numeric entries are omitted because the flattened layout does not reliably assign all values to models and metrics; the paper's explicit qualitative scaling statement is recorded in r35–r36. Cited results from other work in Table 1 and Table 4 are excluded.

untested.parts: No power-law fit, no range spanning orders of magnitude, no token or compute variation; only two unequally trained LM sizes.
Vision models are scaled, but the power-law form is never tested.
No predictive relation to scale or loss is fitted; only 2–3 sizes per setting.

missing.what: Figure 4 bar values for zero-shot ImageNet-1K accuracy are legible: pre-training 52.9/63.6/66.7 and fine-tuning 60.8/69.8/72.3 (B/L/H); ViT-H scores 72.2/79.1.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T2' and its supports labels are overturned. Two-to-three-point gains of the authors' own architecture do not test power-law, predictability or allocation claims. The LM loss comparison is confounded by unequal training completion. Table 5's compute-efficient strategy concerns patch-size curricula, not V3.

versions.untested_parts: Only CRATE-α-small and CRATE-α-base are compared on validation cross-entropy. The study does not fit a power law, test several orders of magnitude, vary training tokens or compute, or establish that other quantities are not bottlenecks.
No predictions from small-run fits are reported.
No fixed-compute search for an optimal parameter/token allocation or compute-dependent allocation trend is reported.
Patch sizes are compared, but the paper does not test whether depth, width, or architecture details change loss only slightly at a fixed parameter count.

The paper scales vision models and reports image-task outcomes, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in vision or another modality. It also does not test the other listed regimes as power-law claims.
The paper reports downstream image-task performance across selected sizes and datasets, but does not fit a predictive relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss or scale.
No comparison of fitted exponents or fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from a power law, is reported.

reader_labels.condition: CRATE-α language models trained autoregressively on OpenWebText
reader_labels.reason: The two reported sizes have validation losses of 3.28 and 3.14, but differ in completed training iterations and do not establish a power law; see r1–r2.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet-1K classification across the reported Base/Large configurations
reader_labels.reason: The larger CRATE-α configurations achieve higher reported top-1 accuracy for the matched patch-size comparisons; see r3–r8.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports higher scores for the larger CRATE-α configurations across CIFAR-10/100, Oxford Flowers-102, and Oxford-IIIT-Pets; see r9–r28.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot ImageNet-1K accuracy in DataComp1B vision-language training
